title: The Musical Composer
philosophicalAnchor: The composer thinks in transformations—map each note higher, filter out the inaudible, reduce to total duration. This is functional programming as musical composition: pipeline the data through pure transformations.
pythonConcept: map, filter, functools.reduce, lambda functions, functional programming, pipeline
briefDescription: Build a digital synthesizer backend using map, filter, and reduce to transform musical note sequences.
theoryPillar: Map applies a function to each element, producing a transformed sequence. Filter removes elements based on a predicate. Reduce accumulates elements into a single result. Together they form a functional pipeline.
anchorPillar: The composer wants to transpose melodies (double frequencies), remove inaudible notes (20-20000 Hz range), and calculate total duration. Each operation is a pure function transforming the data.
triggerPillar: Note dictionaries contain frequency and duration. Transposing doubles frequency. Notes outside human hearing should be discarded. Total track duration requires summing all valid note durations.
realityPillar: map(lambda note: {...}, notes) applies transformations. filter(lambda n: 20 <= n['frequency'] <= 20000, notes) removes invalid notes. reduce(lambda acc, n: acc + n['duration'], notes, 0) sums durations.
